newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: U.S. to test jungle-penetrating sensor device.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to test jungle-penetrating sensor device.

text.p: The U.S. military will test an airborne jungle-penetrating sensor device later this month in an area near Colombia's heavily forested border with Panama, authorities said on Friday.

A statement from the Colombian Defence Ministy said the tests, set to take place "within the next few days," would involve flights over Colombian territory. But the U.S. embassy in Panama issued a statement saying none of the flights would come within more than 20 miles (32 km) of the Colombia-Panama frontier.
The embassy statement said the new sensor technology could facilitate the detection of drug trafficking activity and missing aircrafts in triple-canopy jungle areas.

It did not elaborate, but the sensors could presumably help target leftist guerrilla hideouts in jungles across Colombia, including southwestern Putumayo province where 60 soldiers have been held prisoner by Colombian rebels since Aug. 30.
